findings.summary: The landed placement change reddens a pre-existing test that exercises generate_router_script: test_generated_script_without_the_option_unsets_the_gate_path compares the generated script byte-for-byte against the script produced at revision 268df346 (normalising only the --output line and the removed unset line), and the new placement headers (--partition=rigel instead of betelgeuse, no --reservation) plus the added TMPDIR fallback line break that equality. Verified by running tests/test_agent_gate_control_path.py against an extraction of 466fd4bd: 1 failed, 17 passed, EXIT=1, log /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261027T160701203743-review-of-router-placed-on-rigel-466fd4bd5bac/tests/pre-existing-gate-control-path-at-466fd4bd.log. The file is outside the reviewed node's declared write paths, which is why its gate never saw it; the node lands red until either that comparison is updated (needs a scope grant) or the equality is relaxed to the headers the change legitimately moves.

KNOWN_PARTITIONS hardcodes twelve ITER SDCC partition names into profile.py, and require_known_partition refuses anything outside it with no override, so a site that names its own partition through AMBIX_AGENT_ROUTER or SiteConfig.router cannot generate a router script at all, even though the rest of SiteConfig is site-parameterised. The list is also a snapshot ('sinfo read 2026-10-27') that goes stale silently: a new partition is refused with the same message as a typo.

The generated-headers bullet claims 'A test pins exactly that' for the full unconfigured-site header set (--partition=rigel, --account=grpa, --cpus-per-task=2, --mem=8G, --time=0), but tests/test_agent_router_service.py:test_router_dry_run_requests_the_rigel_partition_without_a_gpu asserts only the partition and the absence of --gres/--nodelist/--constraint; the default account, CPU, memory and time limit, and the absence of --reservation at the default site, are asserted nowhere, so a regression in any of them would leave the fragment's claim standing.
